articles.title: The Shallow Sky
articles.summary: This article provides a guide to the May night sky, detailing the visibility of various planets including Saturn, Mercury, Venus, and Mars, while also highlighting two major astronomical events. It emphasizes the upcoming Venus transit on June 5 and an annular solar eclipse on May 20, providing viewing details, safety precautions (like using solar filters), and optimal locations. The piece also includes a brief report on an amateur astronomer's observation of clouds on Mars and a mention of the Golden State Star Party.

articles.title: Magnetars
articles.summary: The article discusses how seemingly distinct astronomical phenomena, such as magnetars and pulsars, or quasars and blazars, are often later understood as different manifestations of the same underlying object. It elaborates on magnetars as neutron stars with strong magnetic fields, and then details how quasars and blazars are different views of active galactic nuclei (AGN). The text also highlights recent NASA WISE discoveries of many blazars, which are helping to understand the evolution of supermassive black holes and gamma-ray sources.

articles.title: NASA Space Place
articles.summary: Europe's Rosetta mission, with significant NASA contributions, is set to make history by orbiting and landing a probe on comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko to conduct the most comprehensive study ever, aiming to understand the early solar system. Additionally, the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) announced its annual Yosemite Public Star Party in August, offering free admission and camping for participants, alongside regular telescope tune-up sessions held at Houge Park.

articles.title: The Last Month In Astronomy
articles.summary: This article, titled "The Last Month In Astronomy," provides a roundup of astronomy news from March and April 2012. Key updates include new insights into Centaurus A from combined infrared and X-ray data, reports on several close asteroid passes, a mystery cloud observed on Mars, and the potential for comet C/2011 L4 (PANSTARRS) to become a naked-eye object in 2013. Additionally, it covers the controlled deorbiting of the damaged Russian satellite Expres-AM4 and the release of the full WISE infrared space observatory catalog, detailing 560 million celestial objects and aiding in asteroid detection.

articles.title: SETICON II
articles.summary: SETIcon II is a unique public event organized by the SETI Institute, scheduled for June 22-24, 2012, in Santa Clara, CA. It aims to bridge science and imagination by bringing together scientists, science fiction authors, and artists with the public to explore space, real science, and technology. The event features panels, discussions, interactive exhibits, and awards, emphasizing a new channel for dialogue where real science meets imagination, distinct from traditional technical conferences.

articles.title: It Must Be Astronomical ...
articles.summary: This article from the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) announces that all board officers have retained their positions following recent elections. It also informs members about the rescheduling of the annual auction to May 6, 2012, and the temporary suspension of the telescope loaner program for inventory and repair. Additionally, the document provides statistics on completed school star parties and lists future scheduled events, alongside contact and publication information.
